newsitem.title: ROMANIA: TAROM TO SELL SOVIET-BUILT AIRCRAFT BY TENDER.
newsitem.headline: TAROM TO SELL SOVIET-BUILT AIRCRAFT BY TENDER.

text.p: Romania's Tarom SA state airline will sell some of its Soviet-made aircraft in a tender through a local commodities exchange, as part of its major restructuring plan, a company senior executive said on Monday.
"We signed an agreement with the Bucharest commodities exchange to sell some of our Soviet-made planes. The project is in its initial stage," Tarom General Manager Dan Vulcan said.
Vulcan said the documents for the tender would be ready by next week.
He declined to elaborate on the number of aircraft to be sold through the Bursa de Marfuri Bucuresti (BMB) exchange or the minimum starting prices in the planned tender.
But a source with the BMB told Reuters Tarom would offer 20 aircraft, including Antonov-24s, Ilyushin Il-18s and Tupolev Tu-154Bs.
"Tarom also has big amounts of spare parts for these planes. The parts will be part of the package," it said.
To become effective, the project needs approval from the State Ownership Fund, which owns a controlling stake in Tarom.
"I'm confident the tender will be succesful. I know Tarom has been approached by several buyers who showed interest in the deal," the BRB source said without elaborating.
Tarom's Soviet-era fleet include 14 Antonov-24s, four Ilyushin Il-18s and seven Tupolev Tu-154Bs, data show. The planes are in "good shape" and have long hours of service ahead, airline sources said.
The airline's international routes are served by two A-310 Airbus planes, five Boeing 737s and six BAC 1-11 aircraft.

Earlier this month, the Transport Ministry said it would go ahead with plans to restructure the debt-ridden company, including layoffs and sale of its outdated Soviet-made planes, despite opposition from Tarom's trade unions.
Romania's flag carrier faces serious financial problems. Its internal debts total 80 billion lei ($11.1 million) and external debts $15.5 million, according to local media reports.
Tarom plans to buy eight Boeing 737s, to renew its fleet, and hopes to strike a cooperation accord with Trans-World Airlines of the United States.
